clue.text: Eatery has starter of rissoles in gravy

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside another, tucked into the brand name that follows

parts.note: Bisto is a long-established British brand of gravy granules

indicators.note: a starter is the first course, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: opening letter of rissoles

explanation.surface: A restaurant serves rissoles in gravy as its first course.
explanation.walkthrough: Bisto is the famous British gravy brand; the single letter goes inside it after BIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small, informal restaurant, so it is a kind of eatery.

clue.text: Batting side initially happening to get man into safe area is over the moon

indicators.note: one piece is put into another, so it sits inside it

parts.note: a cricket side that is batting is said to be in

indicators.note: initially points to just the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter of side
a happening is an event
a haven is a place of safety
a man is referred to as he

explanation.surface: A batting team is delighted when something happens to get a batsman home safely.
explanation.walkthrough: The man goes in right after the first letter of the safe area, which is why the answer has two H's in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idioms for being blissfully happy and elated.

clue.text: Endlessly groom large dog

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: to groom someone for a role is to train them
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Someone is forever grooming an enormous hound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' looks like the animal in the surface, but here it is a verb, meaning to follow closely.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow or shadow them persistently, which is to trail them.

clue.text: Primate managed to get godhead into published article

indicators.note: these letters are put inside the following words

parts.note: a book that is published is out
an is the indefinite article
to manage a business is to run it; past tense ran

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, attached here to the word god

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of god

explanation.surface: A church leader got a deity's image into a printed piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests an archbishop alongside 'godhead', but it is the ape. RANG sits inside OUTAN, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The orang-utan is a great ape of Borneo and Sumatra, and apes are primates.

clue.text: Snag with Thailand ending revolutionary conflict has Obama losing heart

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter only

parts.note: last letter of Thailand

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns round, so the word is read from the back

parts.note: a war is an armed conflict

indicators.note: the heart is the middle, so the central letters of the name are taken out

parts.note: Barack is Obama's first name

explanation.surface: A political problem: a revolutionary war in Thailand leaves the US president dispirited.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of BARACK is the middle pair RA, which comes out.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is a hidden problem or disadvantage, which is what a drawback is.

clue.text: Imagined setter in fear!

indicators.note: one word sits inside the other, enclosed by the word for terror

parts.note: dread is great fear
the crossword setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: The setter claims to have pictured themself in a state of terror.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often call themselves 'setter' or 'this writer' to mean ME.
explanation.definitionFit: To dream something up is to imagine it, so dreamed is the past tense of that sense.

clue.text: Need to pursue a cry of woe

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the first word comes after the next one

parts.note: taken as written
a need is a lack of something

explanation.surface: Wanting to chase after something makes one cry out in sorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Alack is an old exclamation of regret or sorrow, as in alas and alack.

clue.text: Worst fear is a computer problem to put up with

parts.note: a bug is a fault in a program
to bear something is to tolerate it

explanation.surface: Someone's greatest dread is a computer glitch they must tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugbear is an object of persistent dread or irritation, close to a worst fear.

clue.text: Can't betray rules set out for pilgrims' stories

indicators.note: to set things out is to lay them in a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters of these words, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Those who cannot break the rules have them laid down for pilgrims.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in Can't is ignored, as punctuation always is.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaucer's Canterbury Tales are told by pilgrims riding to the shrine of Thomas Becket.

clue.text: Made non-starter sequel to hit space adventure

indicators.note: a sequel comes after, so the first part is placed behind the second
something hit is knocked about, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: with no starter, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A follow-up to a smash-hit space adventure film was made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit' looks like a box-office success, but it is the shuffle signal for the word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade is a daring or reckless adventure.

clue.text: Paganini endlessly suffering heart disease

indicators.note: something suffering is in a bad way, so its letters are disordered
without ends, so both the first and last letters are removed

parts.note: the Italian violinist's name, taken as written

explanation.surface: The great violinist suffered endlessly from a heart condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Angina is chest pain caused by restricted blood flow to the heart, a form of heart disease.

clue.text: Circle around loo in place where getting runs is likely!

definitions.text: place where getting runs is likely

parts.note: the letter O is circular

indicators.note: turned around, the word is read from back to front

parts.note: lav, short for lavatory, is another word for loo

explanation.surface: A toilet joke: sitting round the loo is where you'd expect to get the runs.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a London cricket ground, where runs are scored; the runs is also slang for diarrhoea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oval is a Test cricket venue, and cricket is the game in which batsmen score runs.

clue.text: He organises shooting sessions with goalie after match

indicators.note: after places the goalie word behind the word for match

parts.note: a match is a game
a goalie is a goalkeeper, or keeper

explanation.surface: A football coach runs shooting practice with the goalkeeper after a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shooting' suggests shots at goal, but it means hunting game birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamekeeper manages an estate's game birds and runs the shoots held there.

clue.text: Creepy-crawly, pointlessly biting fellow, spread disease

indicators.note: biting something holds it between the jaws, so one piece goes inside
with no point, so the letter standing for a compass point is removed

parts.note: a creepy-crawly is an insect
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: A bug that bites a man for no reason passes on an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: S for south is the compass point that comes out of INSECT before F goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: To infect is to pass a disease on to someone, which is how a disease is spread.

clue.text: Identify O'Connor's house by Finisterre

parts.note: Des O'Connor was a long-running British TV host and singer
crib is slang for a home

indicators.note: finis is Latin for the end, so only the final letter of the place name counts

parts.note: the last letter of Finisterre, a Spanish cape

explanation.surface: Pinpoint where Des O'Connor's house is, near Cape Finisterre.
explanation.walkthrough: Finisterre means 'end of the earth', and the setter reads it as the end of the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To describe a thing is to depict it in words, which can identify or characterise it.

clue.text: Cockney chars raised whip-round with brilliance

indicators.note: in a down answer, raised means written from bottom to top
Cockney speakers drop the H at the start of a word

parts.note: chars are cleaning women, also called daily helps

indicators.note: to whip something is to beat it up, so the word after it is scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: East End cleaners held a collection for someone with great style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip-round' looks like one word for a collection, but splits into the signal and its fodder. A char is a British cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendour is magnificent brightness or grandeur, so it means brilliance.

clue.text: Old joke about chicken crossing street even aunt will follow

indicators.note: these letters come after the rest at the end

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: crossing the street here means taking it inside, so it goes into the bird

parts.note: a hen is a chicken
ST is the abbreviation for street

indicators.note: even means the letters in even-numbered places, the second and fourth

parts.note: second and fourth letters of aunt

explanation.surface: Even an aunt will repeat the gag about why the chicken crossed the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface itself cites the most famous chestnut of all.
explanation.definitionFit: A chestnut is a joke or story so stale from retelling that everyone knows it.

clue.text: Deliver TV for nothing

parts.note: a TV is a television set
something for nothing costs nothing, so it is free

explanation.surface: Bring a television round without charging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliver' suggests a courier, but here it means to rescue, as in 'deliver us from evil'.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver someone is to rescue or liberate them from captivity or danger.

clue.text: Drunkard, having left after double parking, got into row

indicators.note: getting into something means going inside it

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

indicators.note: after puts this letter behind the doubled parking symbol

parts.note: P is the parking symbol, doubled here
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A drunk who left the car double-parked then got into a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel, rhyming with cow, but it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A tippler is a habitual drinker, one who tipples, so a drunkard.

clue.text: Remove tab from veritably hideous uniform

indicators.note: hideous means ugly and misshapen, so the remaining letters are put in a new order
removing takes the named letters away from the longer word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Take the label off a truly ugly uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: The T, A and B come out of VERITABLY wherever they sit, leaving six letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A livery is the distinctive uniform worn by servants or members of a guild.

clue.text: Touched by advice on page and print spacing from writer

parts.note: felt is the past tense of feel, to touch
a tip is a piece of advice
P is the abbreviation for page
an en is a printer's unit of space, half an em

explanation.surface: An author is moved by advice on page layout and typesetting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' suggests an author, but it is a thing that writes.
explanation.definitionFit: A felt-tip pen is an instrument for writing, so it is a writer in the literal sense.

clue.text: King aboard rough ride gets irritated

indicators.note: aboard means on board, so one piece is carried inside the other
a rough version is crude and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch on a bumpy journey becomes annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be irked is to be annoyed or irritated.

clue.text: Capable of power in workout

indicators.note: one letter is placed inside the others
to work something is to knead and reshape it, so the letters move

parts.note: the word after the signal work, taken as written
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: Someone is fit enough for a power workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Workout' looks like one word, but splits into the signal and its fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: If you are up to a task, you are able or fit enough to do it.

clue.text: Escort American girl

parts.note: US is short for United States, hence American
a girl is referred to as her

explanation.surface: Someone accompanies a young woman from the States.
explanation.definitionFit: An usher guides people to their seats, so to usher is to escort.

clue.text: Composer from Denmark hosts ball in Victoria and Albert's capital

indicators.note: a host holds others inside, so the code for the country surrounds what follows

parts.note: DK is the international code for Denmark

indicators.note: and simply joins one piece onto the next
the ball sits inside the queen's royal initials

parts.note: VR stands for Victoria Regina, Queen Victoria's royal cipher
a ball is round like the letter O

indicators.note: a capital is a first letter, so only the start of the name is used

parts.note: first letter of Albert

explanation.surface: A Danish composer is staging a ball at the V&A museum in London.
explanation.walkthrough: The V&A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London; here Victoria is her royal cipher VR, with the ball nested inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonín Dvořák was a Czech composer, best known for the New World Symphony.

clue.text: Sneaky way out of swimming baths back to house on banks of lake

indicators.note: on here means placed beside, with the next pieces added after
going back means reading the word from its end to its start

parts.note: a swimming pool
HO is the abbreviation for house

indicators.note: the banks are the edges, so just the outer letters of the word are used

parts.note: first and last letters of lake

explanation.surface: A cheeky escape route from the pool back to a lakeside house.
explanation.definitionFit: A loophole is an ambiguity that lets someone evade a rule, a crafty means of escape.

clue.text: Create purpose in green movement

indicators.note: one word is set inside the other
movement shifts the letters into a different order

parts.note: taken as written
an end is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: Give the environmental movement a sense of purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green movement' reads as environmentalism; it is a word and its shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To engender is to cause or bring something into being, so to create it.

clue.text: Some native deer are strangely the least widely known

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used

parts.note: the letters run across these words, from the end of deer

explanation.surface: Some local deer are oddly the most obscure kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strangely' looks like a shuffle signal, but the letters appear in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare means uncommon or seldom met with, so the rarest is the least commonly known.
